solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Instrument with groan grabbed by second man able to have a good look

definitions.text: able to have a good look

indicators.note: the instrument and the groan are held inside the letters for second and man, as if seized

parts.note: Ted is a man's name
a harp is a stringed instrument
a groan and a sigh are both sounds of weariness

explanation.surface: A man clutching a musical instrument and moaning, apparently straining for a better view.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grabbed by' signals the container: the second-man pair wraps round the instrument and groan.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with keen eyesight is well able to look carefully and spot detail.

clue.text: Loonies in house facing terrible deaths

indicators.note: terrible signals the letters of deaths being mangled

explanation.surface: Madmen in a house facing gruesome ends.
explanation.definitionFit: Impetuous, rash people may loosely be called crazies or madcaps.

clue.text: Dean beginning to row on Welsh river

indicators.note: only the opening letter of row is taken

parts.note: the Usk is a river in South Wales

explanation.surface: A cathedral dean starting to row on a river in Wales.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dean' looks like a churchman; it is the forename of the US statesman.
explanation.definitionFit: Dean Rusk was US Secretary of State in the 1960s, so the first name points to his surname.

clue.text: Occasion for red carpet, say — one to come in sight shortly

parts.note: to say is to state

indicators.note: the numeral one enters the shortened view
shortly means cut short, losing the final letter

parts.note: a vista is a sight or view
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A dignitary's arrival, with someone about to come into view soon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shortly' trims VISTA to VIST, and 'to come in' puts I inside: VIS-I-T.
explanation.definitionFit: An official trip by a head of state is a formal occasion where a red carpet is rolled out.

clue.text: Composer entering Greek store

indicators.note: the composer goes inside the abbreviation for Greek

parts.note: Thomas Arne wrote Rule, Britannia!

explanation.surface: A composer walking into a Greek shop.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to gather and keep, a synonym of storing up.

clue.text: Loftier ground suits plant

indicators.note: ground means crushed or milled, so the letters of loftier are broken up and reformed

explanation.surface: Higher land is suitable for growing a certain plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ground' looks like a noun meaning land; it is the past tense of grind.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a clover-like plant with three-part leaves.

clue.text: Oldster is in a muddle, not knowing which course to take?

definitions.text: not knowing which course to take?

indicators.note: a muddle is a jumble, so the letters of the four words are mixed up

explanation.surface: An elderly person confused and unsure which way to go.
explanation.definitionFit: Indecision leads to delay, and slowness or tardiness results from hesitating over a choice.

clue.text: Immature insect behaving badly, losing tail

indicators.note: the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: caddish means behaving like a cad, ungentlemanly

explanation.surface: A young bug misbehaving and losing its tail.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the larva of the caddis fly, an insect in its juvenile stage.

clue.text: With money, see fantastic seaside all around islands

indicators.note: the rearranged seaside letters surround the money, enclosing it completely
something fantastic is wildly imagined, so the letters of seaside are reshaped

parts.note: tin is old British slang for cash

explanation.surface: An invitation to spend money visiting a wonderful coastline encircling some islands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fantastic' is the anagram signal and 'all around' the container; 'see' is only a link inviting the solver.
explanation.definitionFit: The East Indies is the historical name for the archipelago of South-East Asia, a large group of islands.

clue.text: What's visible from flight? Look thoroughly when you hear

indicators.note: the phrase tells the solver that the words are to be taken as spoken, matching in pronunciation

parts.note: to stare well is to look hard and thoroughly

explanation.surface: A riddle about what one might see from an aeroplane, followed by advice to look carefully.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flight' suggests aircraft, but it is a flight of steps; the shaft they run round is what you see from them.
explanation.definitionFit: A flight of stairs winds round the vertical shaft, which is in view as you climb.

clue.text: Cohabiting partner catching cold gets to sit back in luxury

indicators.note: the partner phrase grabs the abbreviation for cold inside it

parts.note: a live-in lover shares one's home

explanation.surface: A live-in partner who has caught a chill gets to relax at home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'catching' signals the container; the cold letter sits between the two words of the partner phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to enjoy a life of ease and plenty.

clue.text: See 9
May, being cricketer back in the pavilion, fade away

parts.note: Peter May was an England cricket captain of the 1950s
a batsman who has been dismissed returns to the pavilion, being out

explanation.surface: A cricketer named May, dismissed and back in the pavilion, gradually fading from view.
explanation.walkthrough: Peter May was a famous England batsman; the pavilion is a cricket ground's clubhouse, where a dismissed batsman returns.
explanation.definitionFit: To tail off gradually until nothing remains is a synonym of dwindling to an end.

clue.text: What sounds like gong — thus this person is prying

indicators.note: the opening words tell the solver the next word is a match in speech

parts.note: gong is British slang for a medal
so means thus
the setter referring to himself gives me

explanation.surface: A question about what resembles a gong, then a remark about a nosy person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gong' is British slang for a medal or decoration.
explanation.definitionFit: Interfering and nosy are close synonyms of prying into others' affairs.

clue.text: Don't rush making statement about midshipman's action

definitions.meaning: a calming instruction to proceed slowly and carefully
Mr Midshipman Easy is the hero of Captain Marryat's novel, so a remark on what he does could be put this way

explanation.surface: Advice to take things slowly, offered as a comment on a young naval officer's conduct.
explanation.walkthrough: Mr Midshipman Easy is an 1836 naval novel by Frederick Marryat; 'Easy does it' read literally says what Easy does.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom is a familiar plea to go gently and avoid haste.

clue.text: Panic when one edge disappears on the wing

indicators.note: one end letter of the word for panic is lost, here the final one

parts.note: alarm is sudden fear or panic

explanation.surface: Panic setting in as a ledge vanishes beneath someone, perhaps a bird about to fly.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective is a technical term meaning relating to or situated on a wing.

clue.text: Underground explorer keeps ailing, one with gripes

indicators.note: the explorer holds the word for ailing inside

parts.note: a caver explores caves
ailing means ill

explanation.surface: A potholer who keeps getting sick and is full of complaints.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who raises petty objections is a complainer or quibbler.

clue.text: Mathematical point English academic put across the wrong way

indicators.note: the two pieces are laid across the grid in reverse order of letters, backwards

parts.note: a don is a university teacher

explanation.surface: An English lecturer explaining a mathematical idea badly.
explanation.definitionFit: In geometry and graph theory this is a point where lines or branches meet.

clue.text: Expert was injured — acted like an amateur?

parts.note: a dab hand is an expert, so dab alone means expert
to have bled is to have been wounded

explanation.surface: A professional got hurt and behaved like a novice.
explanation.definitionFit: Dipping into an activity casually is what a hobbyist or amateur does.

clue.text: Maid out helping gains approval

indicators.note: out here means put out of order, so the letters of maid are rearranged

parts.note: a ration is a measured helping or portion

explanation.surface: A maid going out to help earns praise.
explanation.definitionFit: Warm regard and esteem amount to favourable approval of someone.

clue.text: Greek island with a castle not entirely visible

indicators.note: only part of the run of words shows the island, which is tucked inside them

explanation.surface: A Greek island with a castle half hidden from view.
explanation.definitionFit: Ithaca is the Ionian island that was Odysseus's home.

clue.text: Violent robber heading off to pursue quiet scholar

indicators.note: the shortened robber follows after the quiet letter

parts.note: P is the musical abbreviation for piano, quiet

indicators.note: the first letter of the word is removed

parts.note: a bandit is an armed robber

explanation.surface: A thug, cut off, chasing a mild-mannered academic.
explanation.definitionFit: In India a learned man or wise teacher is honoured with this title.

clue.text: Group about to meet the stars moves in 'moony' fashion

indicators.note: the reversed group joins up with the constellation, coming after it

parts.note: Libra is a constellation and sign of the zodiac

indicators.note: about signals turning the word for group round

parts.note: a set is a group

explanation.surface: A band turning to face the stars and moving dreamily like lovesick moon-gazers.
explanation.definitionFit: The Moon appears to rock slightly, an effect called libration, so the verb names that oscillating motion.

clue.text: Jar, in essence very large

parts.note: pith is the essential core of something
OS is the clothing abbreviation for outsize

explanation.surface: A jar that is, at heart, enormous.
explanation.walkthrough: OS stands for outsize, a clothing size.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the large earthenware storage vessel of ancient Greece, a kind of jar.

clue.text: Opening payment

definitions.meaning: a tear or gap in fabric
money paid regularly for the use of property

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a split in cloth and a tenant's regular charge to a landlord.

clue.text: Very small handout about to be given to city for sports facility

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the handout word is read backwards

parts.note: the dole is a modest state payment
Rome is the Italian capital city

explanation.surface: A meagre grant being handed to a city to build a sports venue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' reverses DOLE to ELOD; 'to be given to' just joins ROME on.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an arena with a banked track for cycle racing, a sporting venue.

clue.text: Places I pass on the way back

indicators.note: returning reads the letters backwards, so the pieces turn round

parts.note: a col is a mountain pass

explanation.surface: Landmarks someone passes while walking home.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin plural of locus, meaning positions or sites.

clue.text: See Methodist err badly and survive tumultuous experience

indicators.note: something done badly is botched, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Watching a Methodist go astray and coming through a turbulent time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' is only an instruction to look; the anagram uses METHODIST and ERR.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to come safely through a crisis or period of trouble.
